jurisdiction.name: Austin
jurisdiction.notes: City of Austin full-purpose jurisdiction (Travis County). Building, zoning, site plan, sign and alcohol zoning reviews run through Development Services (DSD) and the Austin Build + Connect (AB+C) portal; food permits through Austin Public Health (APH) Environmental Health Services, which also covers unincorporated Travis County. Use the City's Jurisdictions Web Map first: ETJ and county addresses follow different rules. Mobile food vendors have been licensed by Texas DSHS since July 1, 2026; the city still does the fire inspection.

permits.name: Alcoholic beverage zoning review + City Clerk certification of the TABC application
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Development Services (zoning review) + Office of the City Clerk
permits.notes: Start the TABC application in AIMS, get a tracking number from the City Clerk (512-974-2210), then submit it through DSD's Alcoholic Beverage Permits web form (AB+C account required) and pay the zoning review invoice; new zoning review fees took effect Oct. 1, 2026. Once DSD confirms alcohol sales are allowed at the address, the Clerk signs the city certification; the Travis County Clerk certifies the county wet/dry status separately. Sales are barred within 300 ft of a church, school or public hospital, and on-premise sales within 300 ft of a day care unless you hold an FB certificate.
permits.stall_risk: A 300-ft distance conflict needs a City Council waiver after notice and a public hearing, which can add 2–3 months. Measure from the front door to the nearest church, school, hospital or day care before signing the lease.

permits.name: Site Plan Exemption (change of use / small-scale work, before the building permit)
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Development Services – Site Plan Review
permits.notes: A change of use (e.g. retail or office to restaurant) in an existing building usually qualifies for a Site Plan Exemption under LDC §25-5-2 instead of a full site plan. It is not a building permit, but DSD will not approve the commercial building permit without it; up to 10 disciplines may review it. Submit the exemption request form, AB+C ID, owner authorization and a scaled drawing through the web form, pay the invoice, then wait for the emailed decision.

permits.name: Consolidated site plan with Commercial Design Standards (Subchapter E) review
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Development Services – Site Plan Review
permits.notes: New buildings, additions and significant site work need a sealed consolidated site plan that addresses Subchapter E Commercial Design Standards (building placement, sidewalks, connectivity, site amenities, full cut-off exterior lighting), drainage, water quality, trees and utilities. Plans run through a completeness check and multiple review cycles; utility coordination (AULCC) and fee-in-lieu items can add cost. A conditional-use site plan (bar, late hours) also needs a Land Use Commission hearing.
permits.stall_risk: Full site plans routinely take 6–10 months with several correction cycles. Use a civil engineer with recent Austin approvals, request a pre-application meeting, and do not schedule construction until the site plan is released.

permits.name: Conditional Use Permit for a cocktail lounge (bar) use
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Development Services + Planning Commission / Zoning and Platting Commission
permits.notes: Austin's zoning code treats a bar as a 'cocktail lounge', which is a conditional use in many commercial districts (e.g. CS-1) and needs a conditional-use site plan approved at a Land Use Commission hearing, while a restaurant serving alcohol ('restaurant – general') is usually permitted by right. Cocktail lounges are generally not allowed within 300 ft of a church, school or public hospital, and parking separation from townhouse/condo zoning applies. Check the zoning on the property profile map before signing a lease.
permits.stall_risk: Neighborhood plan contact teams can oppose new lounges (some have adopted blanket opposition), pushing hearings back or adding conditions. Meet the contact team and neighbors before filing and get a letter of support.

permits.name: Late-hours alcohol use zoning check (midnight–2 a.m. service near residential)
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Development Services – Zoning / Land Use Commission
permits.notes: Serving alcohol after midnight needs TABC's Late Hours certificate, and Austin's Land Development Code adds local limits: parking for a cocktail lounge or late-hours restaurant must be separated from townhouse/condo or more restrictive zoning (historically 200 ft) unless the commission grants a variance, and where compatibility standards apply a late-hours restaurant can become a conditional use. Most downtown sites clear this at the alcohol zoning review; sites next to residential may need a hearing.

permits.name: Food Enterprise plan review (new or remodeled food establishment)
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Public Health – Environmental Health Services (submitted through Development Services)
permits.notes: Inside the City of Austin the Food Enterprise Plan Review Application goes in with the commercial building permit through DSD; in unincorporated Travis County it goes through the My Health Department portal. Fee $312 for new construction; remodels $221 (under 2,500 sq ft), $266 (2,500–10,000 sq ft) or $312. Include the equipment schedule, finish schedule, menu and plumbing layout so the grease trap and hand sinks are sized in the first round.

permits.name: Food Enterprise operating permit (pre-opening inspection + permit)
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Public Health – Environmental Health Services
permits.notes: Once the space is built to the approved plans, request the pre-opening inspection ($178) in the My Health Department portal; the operating permit is issued only after you pass, and you cannot serve the public before then. City permit fees run $309, $618 or $927 by annual sales and risk tier, renewed annually. A Certified Food Manager must be on site during all hours and posted, and all food handlers need cards within 30 days of hire.
permits.stall_risk: A failed pre-opening inspection (missing hand sink, no hot water, unapproved equipment substitutions) means rescheduling and can cost 1–3 weeks. Walk the space against the approved plans the week before and get any equipment changes approved first.

permits.name: Commercial building permit (tenant finish-out / remodel / change of use / new building)
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Development Services – Commercial Plan Review
permits.notes: Apply through the commercial web form and AB+C. Since July 15, 2026 DSD's published first-review targets run from 5 business days (small projects, incl. finish-outs under 10,000 sq ft with a change of use) to 10 business days (remodels up to 25,000 sq ft) and 20 for larger work, but each correction cycle adds another review and fees apply from the second update. A change of use cannot be done as a revision; it needs its own application citing the site plan exemption number. Trade permits (MEP, hood) are pulled by registered contractors.
permits.stall_risk: Austin is notorious for long review cycles; multiple correction rounds can stretch a 'two-week' review to three months or more. Submit a complete set from an architect with recent Austin restaurant approvals, answer the Master Comment Report point by point, and avoid deferred submittals, which block final inspection and the CO.

permits.name: Certificate of Occupancy for the restaurant / bar use
permits.notes: Issued after every trade permit passes final inspection, including the Austin Fire final and the hood suppression test. You need a CO showing the restaurant or bar use before APH will issue the food permit and before the City Clerk will certify certain alcohol waivers. Assembly occupancies must post the occupant load card at the building final. DSD reports change-of-use reviews dropped to about two weeks after the October 2025 streamlining.

permits.name: Austin Fire Department annual Public Assembly permit (bars with 50+ occupants)
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Fire Department – Fire Marshal's Office / Prevention
permits.notes: AFD requires an annual Public Assembly permit for establishments operating at 50 or more people where alcohol makes up 51% or more of gross sales (bars, lounges, music venues); restaurants below that ratio rely on the posted occupant load from the CO. The property owner or agent applies online, AFD inspects exits, occupant load signage, extinguishers and alarms, and re-inspections are billed hourly. The establishment must already hold its TABC permit.

permits.name: Commercial kitchen hood & suppression system permit and annual fire protection compliance
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Fire Department – Engineering Services / Fire Protection Systems
permits.notes: Type I hoods over grease-producing equipment need a fire suppression system installed by a licensed contractor under its own AFD-reviewed permit, with an acceptance (discharge) test before the building final. After opening, the hood, sprinkler and alarm systems must be inspected by third-party companies that report through The Compliance Engine; AFD's fire code treats these as annual operational permits. Schedule the hood test before the APH pre-opening inspection.

permits.name: Austin Water grease interceptor approval (Industrial Waste / pretreatment)
permits.notes: Every commercial food preparation business in Austin needs an Austin Water-approved grease interceptor; the approval letter specifying size and design is issued through commercial building plan review (no separate application), and traps under 100 gallons are not approved. Do not buy the trap before you have that letter. Traps must be pumped by a permitted hauler at least every three months; drinks-only or prepackaged operations can request a variance.

permits.name: Sign permit (exterior business signage)
permits.notes: One application per sign through AB+C, filed by a contractor with an Outdoor Advertising Registration account; look up your sign district with the city's determination tool first. Freestanding, roof and projecting signs need engineer- or architect-sealed drawings, awning signs need an existing awning building permit, and illuminated signs generate an electrical permit and a 303 Electrical Sign inspection. Historic districts and the Congress Avenue / 6th Street corridors have stricter rules.

permits.name: Outdoor Music Venue (OMV) permit – outdoor amplified sound
permits.issuing_agency: City of Austin – Entertainment Services Group (Music & Entertainment)
permits.notes: Any commercial establishment using sound equipment in a space not fully enclosed by walls and a roof (patio, rooftop, beer garden) needs an annual OMV permit and a sound impact plan setting its dBA/dBC limits and hours. Owners and neighborhood organizations within 600 ft must be notified within 14 days of applying; permits are not issued within 100 ft of residential property. Citywide outdoor cut-offs are 10:30 p.m. Mon–Wed, 11 p.m. Thu and midnight Fri–Sat, later in the Red River and 6th Street/Warehouse districts, and restaurant uses are capped at 70 dBA.
permits.stall_risk: Neighbor objections within 600 ft lead to reduced hours or decibel limits that can undercut a patio-music concept. Do the outreach before applying and design speakers to face away from homes.

permits.name: Sidewalk cafe / street patio permit (public right-of-way)
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Transportation & Public Works – Right-of-Way Management (Public Space Management)
permits.notes: Apply in AB+C under Public Space Management with a notarized application, construction drawings, adjacent owner contacts and photos; allow up to 30 days for review. Fees are an $800 non-refundable permit fee plus $220 per year for sidewalk space and $2,200 per year for each metered parking space used. After approval you post a bond, a notarized maintenance agreement and a resolution of authority; serving alcohol outside requires your TABC permit to cover the area and $1M liquor liability insurance.

permits.name: City of Austin Hotel Occupancy Tax account (11%)
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Financial Services – Hotel Occupancy Tax (Austin Finance Online)
permits.notes: Lodging in the full-purpose city limits collects the City's 11% HOT (9% occupancy + 2% venue project tax) on top of the 6% state tax, which is remitted separately to the Comptroller. Set up an Austin Finance Online account to get a customer number; reports are due quarterly (Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31) even when no tax is owed. Confirm with the Travis County Tax Office whether a county hotel tax also applies to your address.

permits.name: Mobile food vending fire inspection and permit (propane / cooking units)
permits.notes: Required for any truck or trailer with propane or an appliance (including electric) that produces grease-laden vapors; ice cream or coffee units without cooking or propane are exempt. Submit the online MFV permit application (up to 3 business days to process), pay the $222 invoice in AB+C, then pass the inspection; the permit is annual. Common failures are expired extinguisher or suppression tags and incomplete forms. Units in unincorporated Travis County go to the Travis County Fire Marshal instead.

permits.name: Central Preparation Facility (commissary) agreement for mobile food vendors
permits.issuing_agency: Austin Public Health – Environmental Health Services (CPF must hold a Food Enterprise permit)
permits.notes: Austin vendors operate from a Central Preparation Facility (commissary) that holds a current fixed Food Enterprise permit, documented with a signed CPF contract; if you prep food there yourself you may need your own food permit at that location. APH also asks for a restroom facility agreement for the vending site. Commissary rent is a monthly business cost; the fee range shows the cost if you must permit your own CPF kitchen.
